links.outcome: Sensitivity and alarms per detected event of new ML model versus existing situational awareness program
links.effect: DRI sensitivity 53% vs 22% for existing program (p<0.001); 121 vs 276 alarms per detected event; cardiac cohort 73% vs 18%, malignancy cohort 81% vs 27%.
links.quote: The Deterioration Risk Index (DRI) was 2.4 times as sensitive as our existing situational awareness program (sensitivities of 53% and 22%, respectively; p < 0.001) and required 2.3 times fewer alarms per detected event (121 DRI alarms per detected event vs 276 for existing program).

unlisted_practices: Developing separate disease cohort-specific models (cardiac, malignancy, general) rather than a single model
Building the ML model on top of a preexisting situational awareness program

screen.reason: The study develops and pilots a predictive risk model (Deterioration Risk Index) in real inpatient pediatric care and measures patient deterioration events, but it evaluates the overall intervention rather than comparing specific guardrail or deployment practices.
